about: Question styles as independent axes (plans/20-pipeline-efficiency.md, PE-7, D-37). A question is one value on each axis. `draft` draws compatible combinations; `rules` say which values go together. Explanations go into the prompts. `weights`: base weight per value when drawing (default 1); it sets each value's expected share, and values used more than expected are drawn less. The axes say nothing about the players' age: who can answer a question is the difficulty's job.

move.label: what the player has to do

values.identify: name the thing, animal, place or character that is described, shown or played
values.name_concept: describe a key term of the subcategory and ask for its name ("¿cómo se llama cuando la gente se va del campo a la ciudad?" → urbanización)
values.word_meaning: give a word or expression and ask what it means
values.count: an exact number the player can count or reason out (legs, players, strings, sides)
values.estimate: a number the player can't know exactly but can estimate; the wrong options are far apart
values.record: the real-world record holder: biggest, smallest, oldest, fastest… in the world, never just among the four options
values.origin: where it comes from: the country, region or source of a food, invention, animal, word or custom
values.made_of: what it is made of, or what its parts are
values.purpose: what it is for, or what it is used for
values.cause_effect: what happens if…, or why something happens
values.sequence: what comes before or after, what it was called before, what it becomes, or what comes next in a series
values.connection: what three given things have in common
values.analogy: "A es a B como C es a…"
values.odd_one_out: which of the four does NOT belong or is NOT true; the other three share a real-world property
values.who: who made, invented, discovered, said or did it
values.when: the year, century or era it happened

stimulus.label: what the screen shows or plays as part of the question (essential media; anything but none)

values.none: the question works from the text alone; the media is illustrative or decorative
values.photo: a clear photo of the thing; the player names or judges what they see
values.detail: a close-up photo that shows only part of the thing; the player recognises the whole from the part (the game applies no zoom)
values.silhouette: a silhouette or shadow picture of the thing that exists as such on Commons (the game applies no effect)
values.map_outline: the outline of a country, department or region on a map
values.sound: a sound the player recognises: an animal, a single instrument, a natural sound (Commons only, never songs)
values.video: a short clip that is on Wikimedia Commons (NASA, nature, sport, landscapes); never film, TV or game footage

values.riddle: a riddle in the first person: "Tengo…, vivo en…, ¿qué soy?"
values.scenario: an everyday situation the player can picture: "Estás en la cocina y…"
values.completion: complete a saying, a famous line or a well-known phrase
values.three_facts: three short facts that together point to exactly one answer

values.thing: things, animals, plants, foods or objects
values.place: places: countries, cities, regions, landmarks, rivers
values.word: words, terms, names of concepts or short meanings
values.group: groups, families, kinds or categories ("mamíferos", "instrumentos de viento")

lens.label: where the player has met the topic

values.school: what is taught at primary and secondary school
values.university: what is taught at college or university: the basics of a discipline, its classic theories, experiments and textbook examples
values.everyday: home, the kitchen, the street, shopping, work, the things people use every day
values.colombia: Colombian places, food, customs, people or nature
values.pop_culture: films, TV series and shows, games, comics, novels, music and their characters
values.popular_science: popular science books and the famous ideas they made known: thought experiments, paradoxes, well-known experiments and the stories behind discoveries
values.science_news: discoveries, missions and findings that made the news; only settled facts, never current records or anything still changing
values.educational_media: documentaries, educational YouTube channels, science and history TV programmes, museums and planetariums
values.nature: animals, plants, weather and landscapes, outdoors
values.history: how things were long ago, and how they changed
values.body_senses: the human body, the senses, health, sport and movement
values.language: words, names, sayings and where they come from
